title: Present Simple Tense
description: Used for habits, routines, general truths, and permanent situations.
descriptionTr: Alışkanlıklar, rutinler, genel doğrular ve kalıcı durumlar için kullanılır.

Instructions & directions — You **turn** right at the corner.

title: Present Perfect Tense
description: Used for past actions with present relevance, experiences, and unfinished time periods.
descriptionTr: Geçmişteki eylemlerin şimdiki zamana etkisi, deneyimler ve tamamlanmamış zaman dilimleri için kullanılır.
whenToUse: Life experiences — I **have visited** 10 countries.
Recent actions with present results — She **has lost** her keys. (Still looking)
Unfinished time periods — We **have had** 3 meetings this week.
With 'since' and 'for' — He **has lived** here since 2015.
First time / superlative — This is the best book I **have ever read**.

title: If Clauses (Conditionals)
description: Used to talk about conditions and their results — real, unreal, and hypothetical situations.
descriptionTr: Koşullar ve sonuçları hakkında konuşmak için kullanılır — gerçek, gerçek dışı ve varsayımsal durumlar.
whenToUse: Type 0 — General truths: If you heat water, it boils.
Type 1 — Real/possible future: If it rains, I will take an umbrella.
Type 2 — Unreal present: If I had money, I would buy a car.
Type 3 — Unreal past: If I had studied, I would have passed.

structure.positive:
Type 0: If + Present Simple, Present Simple
Type 1: If + Present Simple, will + V1
Type 2: If + Past Simple, would + V1
Type 3: If + Past Perfect, would have + V3
structure.negative:
Type 1: If + don't/doesn't + V1, won't + V1
Type 2: If + didn't + V1, wouldn't + V1
Type 3: If + hadn't + V3, wouldn't have + V3
structure.question: What will you do if ...? / What would you do if ...?

notes.title: Type 0 — Genel Doğruluk

notes.title: Type 1 — Gerçek Olası Durum
notes.description: Gelecekte olması muhtemel durumlar. If + Present Simple, will + V1.
examples: If you **study** hard, you **will pass** the exam.

notes.title: Type 2 — Hayali Şimdiki Zaman
notes.description: Gerçek olmayan, hayal edilen durumlar. If + Past Simple, would + V1. (were her zaman kullanılabilir)
examples: If I **were** rich, I **would travel** the world.
If she **had** time, she **would help** you.

notes.title: Type 3 — Hayali Geçmiş
notes.description: Geçmişte olmamış, pişmanlık/hayal durumları. If + Had + V3, would have + V3.
examples: If I **had studied**, I **would have passed**.
If we **had left** earlier, we **wouldn't have missed** the flight.

title: Passive Voice
description: Used when the action is more important than who does it, or the doer is unknown.
descriptionTr: Eylemin kimin yaptığından daha önemli olduğu veya yapanın bilinmediği durumlarda kullanılır.
whenToUse: Focus on the action — The letter **was sent** yesterday.
Unknown doer — My car **was stolen**.
Formal/academic writing — The experiment **was conducted** in 2023.
Rules & processes — Tickets **are sold** at the entrance.
News reports — Three people **were injured** in the accident.

structureHelp.meaning: In passive, subject RECEIVES the action (not doing it!)
structureHelp.meaningTr: Passive'de özne eylemi YAPAN değil, eylemden ETKİLENEN'dir!
examples: Active: Tom wrote **the letter**. → Passive: **The letter** was written by Tom.

structureHelp.meaning: Changes form based on tense: am/is/are/was/were/been/being
Past participle (3rd form of verb)
The actual doer of the action (optional — often omitted)
structureHelp.meaningTr: Eylemi gerçekten yapan kişi (isteğe bağlı — çoğu zaman yazılmaz)
examples: The cake was baked **by my mom**.
The window was broken. (by kim? bilinmiyor)

notes.title: Tense'e göre passive
notes.description: Her tense'in passive formu farklıdır. 'Be' fiili ilgili tense'e göre çekimlenir.

examples: The window was broken. (by kim? bilinmiyor)

notes.title: Active → Passive dönüşümü
notes.description: Active cümledeki nesne, passive cümlede özne olur.

title: Relative Clauses
description: Used to give extra information about a noun using who, which, that, where, when, whose.
descriptionTr: who, which, that, where, when, whose kullanarak bir isim hakkında ek bilgi vermek için kullanılır.
whenToUse: Define a person — The woman **who lives** next door is a doctor.
Define a thing — The book **which/that** I read was amazing.
Define a place — The city **where** I was born is Istanbul.
Define a time — 2020 was the year **when** everything changed.
Show possession — The man **whose** car was stolen called the police.

title: Too & Enough
description: Used to express excess (too) or sufficiency (enough) with adjectives, adverbs, and nouns.
descriptionTr: Sıfat, zarf ve isimlerle aşırılık (too) veya yeterlilik (enough) ifade etmek için kullanılır.
whenToUse: Excess — The coffee is **too** hot to drink.
Sufficiency — She is old **enough** to drive.
Insufficiency — He isn't tall **enough** to reach it.
With nouns — We don't have **enough** time.

notes.title: too vs very

examples: She is **very** tall. (sadece vurgu, sorun yok)

title: Past Continuous Tense
description: Used for actions that were in progress at a specific time in the past.
descriptionTr: Geçmişte belirli bir anda devam etmekte olan eylemler için kullanılır.
whenToUse: Actions in progress at a past time — I **was reading** at 9 PM.
Interrupted actions — She **was cooking** when the phone rang.
Parallel actions — While I **was studying**, he **was sleeping**.
Setting the scene — The sun **was shining** and birds **were singing**.

title: Present Perfect Continuous
description: Used for actions that started in the past and are still continuing, or recently stopped with visible results.
descriptionTr: Geçmişte başlayıp hâlâ devam eden ya da yakın zamanda bitip etkisi görülen eylemler için kullanılır.
whenToUse: Duration up to now — I **have been studying** English for 3 years.
Recent activity with evidence — You're wet! **Have** you **been swimming**?
Temporary ongoing action — She **has been working** here since January.
Repeated recent actions — He **has been calling** me all day.
Emphasizing duration — They **have been waiting** for two hours!

structure.negative: Subject + have/has + not + been + V-ing + Object
structure.question: Have/Has + Subject + been + V-ing + Object?

structureHelp.meaning: have been (I/you/we/they), has been (he/she/it)

title: Used to / Would (Past Habits)
description: Used to talk about past habits, states, and repeated actions that no longer happen.
descriptionTr: Artık yapılmayan geçmiş alışkanlıklar, durumlar ve tekrarlanan eylemler için kullanılır.
whenToUse: Past habits — I **used to** play football every weekend.
Past states — She **used to** live in Paris.
Repeated past actions — We **would** always go to the beach in summer.
Contrast past & present — I **used to** hate vegetables, but now I love them.
Nostalgic memories — We **used to** play outside all day as kids.

structure.positive: Subject + used to + V1 / Subject + would + V1
structure.question: Did + Subject + use to + V1?

structureHelp.meaning: For past habits AND states (no longer true)

structureHelp.meaning: For repeated past ACTIONS only (not states)
structureHelp.meaningTr: Sadece tekrarlanan geçmiş EYLEMLER için (durumlar için kullanılmaz)

title: Prepositions of Time (in, on, at)
description: Used to express when something happens — with times, days, months, seasons, and years.
descriptionTr: Bir şeyin ne zaman olduğunu ifade etmek için kullanılır — saatler, günler, aylar, mevsimler ve yıllar ile.

title: Phrasal Verbs
description: Verbs combined with prepositions or adverbs that create a completely new meaning different from the original verb.
descriptionTr: Edatlar veya zarflarla birleşerek orijinal fiilden tamamen farklı bir anlam oluşturan fiiller.
whenToUse: Daily routines — I **wake up** at 7 AM.
Relationships — They **broke up** last month.
Actions — Please **turn off** the lights.
Discovery — I **found out** the truth.
Continuation — **Keep on** trying, don't give up!

structureHelp.meaning: Object can go between the verb and the particle
structureHelp.meaningTr: Nesne fiil ile edat arasına girebilir

structureHelp.meaning: Object MUST come after the whole phrasal verb
structureHelp.meaningTr: Nesne tüm öbeksi fiilin SONRASINA gelmelidir

structureHelp.meaning: With pronouns (it, them), separable verbs MUST be split
structureHelp.meaningTr: Zamirlerle (it, them) ayrılabilir fiiller AYRILMAK ZORUNDADIR

notes.title: Yaygın phrasal verb'ler (ezberlenmeli!)
notes.description: give up = vazgeçmek, look for = aramak, find out = keşfetmek, put off = ertelemek, turn on/off = açmak/kapatmak, get up = kalkmak, take off = çıkarmak/kalkmak, look after = bakmak, run out of = tükenmek, come across = rastlamak.

notes.title: Zamir kuralı çok önemli!
notes.description: Separable phrasal verb + zamir → zamir ORTAYA girer. Turn off it ✗ → Turn it off ✓.

notes.title: Anlam değişimleri
notes.description: Aynı fiil farklı parçacıklarla çok farklı anlamlar alır!

title: Future Perfect Tense
description: Used to describe actions that will be completed before a specific point in the future.
descriptionTr: Gelecekte belirli bir noktadan ÖNCE tamamlanmış olacak eylemleri anlatmak için kullanılır.
whenToUse: Completed before future point — By 5 PM, I **will have finished** my work.
Duration up to future point — By next month, she **will have lived** here for 10 years.
Achievement — By December, he **will have saved** $5000.
Predictions about completion — The guests **will have arrived** by 8.
Deadlines — I **will have submitted** the report before Friday.

structureHelp.meaning: Auxiliary combination for future perfect — signals completion in the future
structureHelp.meaningTr: Gelecek bitmiş zamanın yardımcı fiil birleşimi — gelecekte tamamlanmayı işaret eder

structureHelp.meaning: Past participle — the third form of the verb
examples: go → gone, eat → eaten, finish → finished
write → written, see → seen, do → done

notes.title: Future Perfect vs Future Simple
notes.description: Future Simple = gelecekte yapacağım. Future Perfect = gelecekteki bir noktadan ÖNCE bitirmiş olacağım.
examples: I **will have finished** it by tomorrow. (yarına kadar bitirmiş olacağım)

notes.title: 'by' anahtar kelimedir
notes.description: Future Perfect neredeyse her zaman 'by' (…e kadar) ile birlikte kullanılır.
examples: **By** the time you arrive, we **will have** left.

notes.title: by the time + Present Simple
notes.description: 'by the time' den sonra Present Simple gelir, Future tense DEĞİL.
examples: By the time you **get** here, I will have finished. ✓
By the time you **will get** here ... ✗

title: Past Perfect Continuous
description: Used to describe actions that were ongoing for a period of time before another past event.
descriptionTr: Geçmişte başka bir olaydan ÖNCE bir süre boyunca devam etmekte olan eylemleri anlatır.
whenToUse: Duration before a past event — She **had been waiting** for 2 hours when the bus came.
Cause of a past result — He was tired because he **had been running**.
Emphasis on duration — They **had been living** there for 5 years before they moved.
Background activity — It **had been raining** all morning, so the roads were wet.
Interrupted actions — I **had been sleeping** when the phone rang.

structureHelp.meaning: Auxiliary for past perfect continuous — links to an earlier past period
structureHelp.meaningTr: Geçmiş bitmiş sürekli zamanın yardımcısı — daha önceki geçmiş döneme bağlar

structureHelp.meaning: Present participle — shows the action was ongoing
structureHelp.meaningTr: Şimdiki ortaç — eylemin devam ettiğini gösterir

notes.title: Past Perfect vs Past Perfect Continuous
notes.description: Past Perfect (had + V3) = eylemin tamamlandığını vurgular. Past Perfect Continuous (had been + V-ing) = eylemin SÜRESİNİ vurgular.
examples: I **had read** 3 books before the trip. (kaç tane — tamamlanmış)
I **had been reading** for 2 hours. (ne kadar süre — süreç)

notes.title: Sonuç görünür!
notes.description: Past Perfect Continuous genelde geçmişteki bir sonucun NEDENİNİ açıklar.
examples: Her eyes were red. She **had been crying**.
The ground was wet. It **had been raining**.
He was out of breath. He **had been running**.

notes.title: Stative verb'ler dikkat!
notes.description: know, believe, want gibi durum fiilleri continuous almaz → Past Perfect kullanılır.
examples: I **had known** her for years. ✓ (durum fiili)
I **had been knowing** her for years. ✗

examQuestions.explanation: 'know' durum fiilidir → continuous almaz → had known.

title: Causative (have/get something done)
description: Used when someone else does something for us — we arrange or cause the action to happen.
descriptionTr: Bir işi başka birine yaptırdığımızda kullanılır — eylemi ayarlarız veya yaptırırız.
whenToUse: Service by professionals — I **had my hair cut** yesterday.
Arranging something — She's **getting her car repaired**.
Delegating tasks — The boss **had the report written** by his assistant.
Negative experience — He **had his wallet stolen**. (unpleasant event)
Persuading — I **got him to help** me with the project.

structureHelp.meaning: Formal / neutral — arrange for something to be done
structureHelp.meaningTr: Resmi / nötr — bir şeyin yapılmasını ayarlamak

structureHelp.meaning: Informal / more effort involved
structureHelp.meaningTr: Gayri resmi / daha fazla çaba gerektiren

structureHelp.meaning: Persuade someone to do something
structureHelp.meaningTr: Birini bir şey yapmaya ikna etmek

structureHelp.meaning: Instruct someone to do something (formal/authority)
examples: The teacher **had** the students **write** an essay.

notes.title: Active vs Causative
notes.description: Active = sen yaparsın. Causative = başkası yapar (sen yaptırırsın).
examples: I **cut** my hair. (Kendim kestim — makas elimde!)
I **had** my hair **cut**. (Kuaföre gittim, kuaför kesti.)

notes.title: Tüm tense'lerde kullanılır
notes.description: have/get fiili tense'e göre çekimlenir, yapı aynı kalır.
examples: Present: I **have** my car **serviced** every year.
Future: I **will have** my car **serviced** next week.
Present Perfect: I **have had** my car **serviced** recently.

notes.title: Olumsuz deneyimler (had sth stolen/broken)
notes.description: have + object + V3 ayrıca istem dışı olumsuz olaylar için de kullanılır.
examples: She **had** her bag **stolen** on the bus. (Çantası çalındı)
He **had** his window **broken** by the storm. (Fırtına camı kırdı)

examples.label: have + O + V3
examples.english: I **had** my hair **cut** at the new salon.

examples.label: get + O + V3
examples.english: She **got** her phone **repaired** last week.

examples.label: get + person + to V1
examples.english: I **got** my brother **to help** me move.
examples.turkish: Kardeşimi taşınmama yardım etmeye ikna ettim.

examples.label: have + person + V1
examples.english: The manager **had** his team **prepare** the presentation.

examples.label: Negative experience
examples.english: He **had** his wallet **stolen** at the market.

examples.label: Future
examples.english: We're **going to get** the house **painted** next month.

commonMistakes.explanation: have/get + object + V3 (past participle) — washing değil washed.

commonMistakes.wrong: I got him help me.
commonMistakes.correct: I got him to help me.
commonMistakes.explanation: get + person + TO + V1 — 'to' gerekli.

commonMistakes.wrong: I had him to write the report.
commonMistakes.correct: I had him write the report.
commonMistakes.explanation: have + person + V1 (to olmadan) — get ile karıştırılmamalı.

title: Inversion (Formal Emphasis)
description: Reversing the normal subject-verb order for emphasis, mostly in formal writing and after certain negative/restrictive adverbs.
descriptionTr: Vurgu için normal özne-fiil sırasını tersine çevirmek — genellikle resmi yazıda ve belirli olumsuz/kısıtlayıcı zarflardan sonra.
whenToUse: After negative adverbs — **Never have** I seen such beauty.
After hardly/scarcely — **Hardly had** she arrived when it started to rain.
After not only — **Not only does** he sing, but he also dances.
After only — **Only then did** I realize my mistake.
Conditionals without if — **Had** I known, I would have come. (= If I had known)

structure.positive: Negative adverb + auxiliary + Subject + main verb
structure.negative: Not only + auxiliary + Subject + verb, but also ...
structure.question: (Already inverted — resembles question form)

structureHelp.meaning: When a negative word starts the sentence, the subject and auxiliary swap
structureHelp.meaningTr: Olumsuz bir kelime cümle başındaysa, özne ve yardımcı fiil yer değiştirir

structureHelp.meaning: Conditional inversion — 'if' is dropped, auxiliary comes first
structureHelp.meaningTr: Koşul cümlesi devrikleri — 'if' düşer, yardımcı fiil öne gelir
examples: **Had** I known ... (= If I had known)
**Were** she here ... (= If she were here)
**Should** you need help ... (= If you should need help)

notes.title: Ne zaman inversion kullanılır?
notes.description: Olumsuz/kısıtlayıcı zarf cümle BAŞINDA olduğunda inversion yapılır. Cümle ortasındaysa normal düzen devam eder.
examples: **Never have** I seen this. (inversion — never başta)
I have **never** seen this. (normal — never ortada)

notes.title: No sooner ... than / Hardly ... when
notes.description: Bu yapılar çifttir ve her zaman birlikte kullanılır.
examples: **No sooner had** I sat down **than** the phone rang.
**Hardly had** she left **when** it started raining.

notes.title: Koşul cümlelerinde inversion
notes.description: 'if' düşürülür ve yardımcı fiil cümle başına gelir. Yazılı ve resmi İngilizce'de sıktır.
examples: **Had** I known, I would have helped. (= If I had known)
**Were** I you, I'd accept. (= If I were you)
**Should** you require anything, please call. (= If you should require)

examples.label: Never
examples.english: **Never have** I tasted such delicious food.
examples.turkish: Hiçbir zaman bu kadar lezzetli yemek tatmadım.

examples.label: Not only ... but also
examples.english: **Not only does** she speak French, **but** she **also** speaks Japanese.
examples.turkish: Sadece Fransızca konuşmuyor, aynı zamanda Japonca da konuşuyor.

examples.label: No sooner ... than
examples.english: **No sooner had** we left **than** it started to rain.
examples.turkish: Biz çıkar çıkmaz yağmur yağmaya başladı.

examples.label: Conditional (had)
examples.english: **Had** I known about the meeting, I would have attended.

examples.label: Rarely
examples.english: **Rarely does** one see such dedication.

examples.label: Hardly ... when
examples.english: **Hardly had** she finished speaking **when** the audience applauded.

commonMistakes.correct: Never have I seen such a thing.
commonMistakes.explanation: Cümle başında olumsuz zarf → auxiliary + subject (devrik düzen).

commonMistakes.wrong: Not only she speaks French, but also Japanese.
commonMistakes.correct: Not only does she speak French, but she also speaks Japanese.
commonMistakes.explanation: Not only + auxiliary + subject + verb yapısı gerekir.

commonMistakes.wrong: No sooner had we left when it rained.
commonMistakes.correct: No sooner had we left than it rained.
commonMistakes.explanation: No sooner → than ile eşleşir (when değil). Hardly → when ile eşleşir.
